About the Founder

KGOPUTŠHO JOHN KGALEMA

Founder. Entrepreneur. Supply Chain Management Student. Data Analyst. Technology & Youth Development Advocate.

Kgoputšho John Kgalema is a South African entrepreneur, student, data analyst, tutor, consultant and community builder whose work sits at the intersection of business, technology, education, supply chain management and youth development.

He is currently pursuing a BCom in Supply Chain Management at the University of Pretoria, following his earlier studies in Information Science. This combination of business and information-oriented education has shaped his approach to problem-solving: understanding how people, information, resources and systems interact, and then finding practical ways to make those systems work better.

His professional interests and experience extend across data analysis, financial oversight, procurement, strategic sourcing, cost optimisation, operational coordination and governance.

Through his work at Kgalema Tutoring Services, he has developed financial and attendance systems, revenue dashboards, expense-monitoring processes and demand-tracking tools designed to improve operational efficiency.

His work has included reducing administrative workload, improving cash-flow visibility, strengthening reconciliation and identifying procurement savings through structured supplier comparison and purchasing analysis.

His CV documents experience in budgeting, procurement and cost optimisation, financial reporting and internal controls, Excel dashboards and automation, data analysis and forecasting, strategic sourcing and supplier evaluation.

However, Kgoputšho's ambitions extend beyond conventional business.

He believes that education is one of the most powerful mechanisms through which a young person can change the trajectory of their life — but access to education, technology, mentorship and opportunity remains unequal.

This belief is one of the foundations behind Phakama Mtanami.

“Talent should never be limited by circumstance.”

The Premise

At the centre of Kgoputšho's work is a belief that young people should not merely be prepared to enter an existing world. They should be equipped with the knowledge, confidence, technical skills, entrepreneurial mindset and networks required to build the world they want to live in.

The Method

This philosophy influences both his business and community-development work. A learner struggling academically may need tutoring — but they may also need mentorship, structure, resources and someone who believes in their potential. A business struggling with costs may need better data, stronger procurement processes, improved forecasting and more disciplined financial controls — not simply a cheaper supplier.

The Systems View

A young person interested in technology may need more than access to a computer; they may need someone to teach them how to turn technology into a skill — and eventually turn that skill into an opportunity. This systems-oriented approach is at the heart of Kgoputšho's work.

Business Ecosystem

NEXIGIMUS

IT & Supply Chain Solutions

Nexigimus is a technology and supply-chain solutions company focused on developing practical, technology-driven solutions to modern operational and supply-chain challenges.

Kgoputšho is a founder and CEO within Nexigimus. The company explores the intersection of information technology, supply chain management, data, digital solutions, business processes, automation, innovation and technology-enabled problem-solving.

Nexigimus is not simply a technology company for the sake of technology. Its philosophy is deliberate and applied:

STEP 01

Identify the problem

STEP 02

Understand the system

STEP 03

Design the solution

STEP 04

Implement

STEP 05

Measure the result

Artificial intelligence is one area of Nexigimus's technological interest — the broader identity of the company remains IT + Supply Chain Solutions.

The Organisation

PHAKAMA MTANAMI

RISE. LEARN. BUILD. IMPACT.

A youth-development initiative focused on education, skills, technology, mentorship and opportunity.

Phakama Mtanami is a community-driven youth-development initiative built around the belief that young people should have meaningful access to education, mentorship, technology, skills development and opportunity regardless of their circumstances.

The organisation seeks to connect young people with the knowledge, skills, support and networks required to participate meaningfully in the future economy.

Phakama Mtanami is not being built as a once-off project. It is being developed as an ecosystem.
“

Your circumstances are not your ceiling.

Phakama Mtanami believes that development should not stop at academic assistance. A young person needs knowledge, skills, mentorship, discipline, technology, networks and opportunity. The organisation therefore seeks to connect these elements into one ecosystem.

Programmes

THE SIX PILLARS OF PHAKAMA

Six interlocking areas of development, designed to work as one system rather than six disconnected services.

01 — EDUCATION

Accessible academic support

Affordable and accessible tutoring and academic support for learners.

02 — SKILLS DEVELOPMENT

Practical, future-facing skills

Practical skills that prepare young people for university, employment, entrepreneurship and the future economy.

03 — TECHNOLOGY

Digital capability

Exposure to digital tools, information technology, data and emerging technologies.

04 — MENTORSHIP

People who develop people

Connecting young people with people who can guide, challenge, encourage and develop them.

05 — ENTREPRENEURSHIP

Commercial thinking

Teaching young people to identify problems, think commercially and develop solutions.

06 — COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

From individual to collective

Turning individual development into collective progress and building stronger communities through collaboration.

The Bigger Vision

THIS IS BIGGER THAN ONE ORGANISATION.

The long-term vision is to build an ecosystem where education, technology, entrepreneurship and community development reinforce one another.

A learner should be able to enter through tutoring.
A student should be able to develop practical skills.
A young entrepreneur should be able to access mentorship.
A technology enthusiast should be able to develop technical capability.
A business should be able to partner with young people and communities.
And eventually, those who benefited from the ecosystem should be able to return and build it for the next generation.

That is the cycle. That is the vision.

“

My mission is not simply to succeed. It is to build systems, businesses and communities that make success more accessible to others.”

The question is not simply: “How far can I go?”

It is: “How many people can rise because I chose to build something?”

Call to Action

RISE WITH US.

Whether you are a learner looking for support, a mentor ready to give back, an organisation looking to create impact, a business looking for meaningful community engagement, or a young person ready to build something — there is a place for you within the ecosystem.
